messages:
Anna (People Ops): Quick note — dropping a tiny pack of 'anchor' phrases folks can copy into self-reviews. Keep each line 1–2 sentences. Aim: clear impact + brief context. Use as-is or tweak.

Devin (Eng Manager): super helpful. can we get 1-line examples for "committed" vs "stretch" work?

Anna (People Ops): yes — here's a tiny playground, feel free to paste:
```
Committed: Delivered X feature that reduced median inference latency by 18% by optimizing batching and KV-cache usage; owned rollout and monitoring.
Stretch: Led cross-team initiative to prototype dynamic routing across 2 model families, enabling 37% cost-per-request reduction in peak windows; proof-of-concept + stakeholder syncs.
``` 

Marco (Senior IC): can you add a manager-friendly micro-feedback snippet? copy/paste for 1:1s.

Anna (People Ops): Manager snippets (1 line each):
```
Observed: Delivered reliably on Q2 commitments and improved latency by 18% — great operational ownership.
Coaching: Continue pairing on cross-team design to scale the routing proof into production; recommend 2 small experiments next sprint.
Praise: Strong sense of ownership and clear updates in standups — big help for the team.
``` 

Li (Manager): Nice. Any guidance on mentioning metrics vs qualitative impact? What's preferred in calibration?

Anna (People Ops): short answer: include metrics when they exist, else use a concise qualitative outcome + user/customer/partner impact. For calibration rounds we prefer a single measurable stat when possible. Also add an explicit timezone for dates if you reference timelines.

Devin (Eng Manager): Can we get a tiny template for the top-summary paragraph (for managers to paste into calibration doc)?

Anna (People Ops): Sure — suggested 2-sentence manager summary:
```
[Name] met their committed goals, improving [metric] by [X%] and reducing incident volume by [Y%]. Recommendation: Promote readiness for next-level responsibilities / continue to develop cross-team leadership (pick one concrete action).
```

Marco (Senior IC): Love the brevity. Any 'don’t' bullets we should avoid in self-reviews?

Anna (People Ops): Yes — avoid vague verbs ("helped", "supported") without context, avoid long lists of tasks without outcome, and don't write in third-person. Keep it actionable.

PeopleOpsBot: Reminder — self-review window closes in 7 days: https://redwood.example.com/perf-cycle (use team templates). :calendar:

Devin (Eng Manager): Awesome pack — will paste in my teams' 1:1s. :thumbsup:

Li (Manager): Thanks, Anna. small ask: can you pin this in the people-ops channel and add a short doc link?

Anna (People Ops): Done — pinned and added to the People Ops self-review playbook. Will follow up with a 5-min drop-in Q&A session invite. :sparkles:
